key_insight: Compress each highly informative frame into a single learned token so large language models can process very long videos without losing key temporal information, enabling extreme token reduction with minimal performance loss.
problem_solved: Addresses the scalability bottleneck of vision–language models on long videos caused by huge per-frame token counts and limited LLM context, which forces sparse sampling and loses temporal cues.
method: Selective frame scoring: identify a small set of highly informative frames from the full video using learned or heuristic importance metrics.
Per-frame extreme compression: convert each selected frame into a single compact token via a learnable visual tokenizer/pooled embedding that preserves semantic and temporal signals.
Train end-to-end (or with distillation/objective constraints) so the compressed tokens retain downstream task performance while reducing token budget to ~1 token/frame at the LLM input.
impact: Enables efficient, scalable long-video understanding with existing LLM backbones by drastically reducing token load, lowering compute and memory costs while maintaining temporal awareness—useful for video QA, summarization, and retrieval at scale.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: full-frame sequence → selective frame scorer → one-token-per-frame tokenizer → LLM
Bar chart: token count and compute vs. baseline (dense tokens) with accuracy trade-off

Architecture block: single-frame tokenizer / pooling module that maps an image to one compact token
paper_title: One Token per Highly Selective Frame: Towards Extreme Compression for Long Video Understanding
paper_authors: Zheyu Zhang, Ziqi Pang, Shixing Chen, Xiang Hao, Vimal Bhat
